problems.statement: The 20-closes-per-day quota with leaderboard consequences is the main cause of the backlog growth: it rewards gaming (premature solves, ticket splitting, cherry-picking quick wins), so closes rise while real resolution falls, producing reopens, duplicates and split children that inflate volume.
Cherry-picking easy tickets has left complex tickets aging and piling up, and these are not being worked, which hurts key customers.

Agents are not putting in the work or the bar is too soft (the client's framing): hourly capacity is unchanged and closes per day nearly reached the target (19.0), so the problem is what counts as a close, not effort.
Underlying demand and capacity shortfall (Payroll launch and under-staffing) explains the backlog doubling, so 12 more agents are the fix.
The reopen-rate rise is an artifact of an auto-reopen-on-reply rule change that counts courtesy replies.
Attrition and the Corvane pay competitor and deferred pay review contribute some staffing and morale strain, but headcount and hours were essentially flat so it does not explain the backlog.
Product or engineering bugs (bank-feed API change) contribute to the aging of complex tickets and may be a real secondary driver of backlog that the quota hides.
Reopened, duplicate and split-child tickets, driven by the quota, have displaced original tickets in the backlog, so the apparent volume surge is mostly self-generated rework.

causalClaims.from: Daily close quota with leaderboard consequences
causalClaims.to: Gaming behaviours (premature solves, splitting, quick-win picking)
Higher reopen rate and customer duplicates
Inflated ticket creation and backlog growth

actions.action: Replace the raw close quota with resolution-based measures (first-contact resolution, no reopen within 14 days, aging-weighted work), stop counting reopened solves and split children as closes, and suspend the leaderboard.
actions.rationale: It removes the incentive that generates the rework and does not depend on any unconfirmed explanation; Team C's partial change cut reopens from 24% to 10%.

actions.action: Restore oldest-first or complexity-weighted queue picking and run a targeted sprint on the aged complex tickets, with Tier 2 and a clear owner.
actions.rationale: Complex tickets and key accounts like Larkspur are aging and at renewal risk, and this is cheap and reversible.

actions.action: Merge duplicates and split children, and proactively contact customers with repeated reopens.
actions.rationale: A large part of the backlog is rework tickets that can be consolidated without new headcount.

actions.action: Tag aged complex tickets that are linked to open engineering bugs and set up a joint escalation path with Integrations.
actions.rationale: It resolves the main unknown cheaply and bank-feed bugs may block resolution regardless of agent behaviour.
Capacity was unchanged and demand rose only about 4% in first-contact issues; the permanent $744k cost is irreversible within the year and extra agents under the same quota would add more gaming.

actions.action: Make the quota tougher with real consequences.
actions.rationale: It would intensify the gaming, reopens and attrition risk that already caused the backlog growth.

actions.action: Revisit the 12-agent request after the metric change has run for 6-8 weeks and the cleaned backlog is measured.
actions.rationale: Genuine capacity need can only be judged once rework is stripped out.

actions.action: Review pay position and accelerate the pay review for agents.
actions.rationale: Competitor pay and 58% leaving intent are a retention risk, though not shown to cause the backlog.

nextEvidence: Number of aged complex tickets linked to open engineering bugs (link check of the 430 tickets) to size the real engineering-dependency share
Backlog and reopen rate after switching metrics, by team, with a comparison of Team C and the Billing-Compliance pod over 6-8 weeks
Cleaned backlog count after merging duplicates and split children, with true workload and capacity per agent-hour to size any genuine staffing gap
output.summary: The backlog doubling is mainly self-inflicted. The close quota with leaderboard pressure rewards gaming: premature solves, ticket splitting and quick-win cherry-picking. Reopens (6% to 23%), duplicates and split children grew about 10x, and by 31 Oct they made up most of the backlog. Capacity was flat, first-contact demand rose only 4%, and Payroll is a small share. The pod without a quota stayed stable, and Team C's partial fix cut reopens. Replace the quota with resolution-based measures and clear aged complex tickets. Do not toughen the target or approve a permanent 12-agent spend yet. Engineering bugs and attrition are secondary uncertainties.
